mods.reason: Breath of the Wild reads one mod folder with a manifest, but a mod that makes a game file larger also needs a matching resource size table, which Graft can't build yet.

files.label: Game app
files.summary: The Mac app MacNativeGames built for Breath of the Wild.
files.detail: Play opens this app. It's named Breath of the Wild.app, and MacNativeGames puts it next to your game file unless you chose another folder when building (for example ~/Games/macOS).

files.label: Base game
files.summary: Your copy of the game itself: the XCI or NSP file you dumped from your Switch.
files.detail: A 1.6.0 card image (XCI) holds the base game, its update and the add-on content in one file. For 1.9.0, MacNativeGames builds from the base game NSP and the 1.9.0 update. Reading it needs the keys from your Switch.

files.label: Update
files.summary: Your copy of the game's update: the 1.6.0 or 1.9.0 update you dumped from your Switch.
files.detail: The game app runs the version of this update. A 1.6.0 card image already holds its update, so you need this file only when your game file is the base game alone.

files.label: Work folder
files.summary: The folder MacNativeGames worked in when it built the game app.
files.detail: It's named BotW_build and sits next to your game file unless you chose another folder when building. It holds the extracted game and the Python environment MacNativeGames builds with.
